title: How can I make a feature request?
content: **Question** How can I make a feature request? **Answer** We have a Product Feedback forum dedicated to collect users' feedback on our program. To submit a feature request, please click [here](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/community/topics/115000546428-Product-Feedback).
content_description: This web page provides guidance on how to submit a feature request through our dedicated Product Feedback forum.

title: Where can I find information on new features of CLO?
content: **Question** Where can I find information on the new features of CLO? **Answer** You can find information about the new CLO features on the following page: <https://www.clo3d.com/en/clo/features>

title: Is there a CLO manual available?
content: **Question** Is there a CLO manual available? **Answer** The manual for CLO is available in [English](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/categories/115000064648-Manual), [Korean](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/categories/115000064648-Manual), [Chinese](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/zh-cn/categories/115000064648-Manual), and [Japanese](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ja/categories/115000064648-Manual). title: Can I import/export OBJ, FBX, Alembic files?
content: **Question** Can I import/export OBJ, FBX, Alembic files? **Answer** All OBJ, FBX, and Alembic files can be imported or exported to CLO. For further information on CLO's compatibility, please refer to the manual, [Compatible File Format](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002000227).
content_description: This webpage provides information on the import and export capabilities of OBJ, FBX, and Alembic files in CLO, along with a link to the compatibility manual.

title: What kind of 3D formats can be imported/exported to and from CLO?
content: **Question** What kind of 3D formats can be imported/exported to and from CLO? **Answer** Please refer to the manual, [Compatible File Format](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002000227), to find the list of compatible 3D files.
content_description: This webpage provides information on the 3D file formats that can be imported and exported in CLO, directing users to the manual for a comprehensive list.

title: How can I check my computer specification?
content: **Question** How can I check my computer specification? **Answer** To check your computer specification, please follow the guideline below: 1. Press the Windows + R keys on your keyboard simultaneously, and type "dxdiag" without the quotes. 2. Press the Enter key or click the 'OK' button. 3. Choose 'Save All Information' at the bottom of the window. 4. Save it as a text file.
content_description: This webpage provides a simple step-by-step guide for users to check their computer specifications using the DirectX Diagnostic Tool.

title: Does any universities offer courses in CLO?
content: **Question** Does any universities offer courses in CLO? **Answer** We partner with various academic institutions worldwide. Please refer to our [Clients](https://www.clo3d.com/business/business_clients) page for more information.
content_description: Discover universities offering courses in CLO and learn about our partnerships with academic institutions globally.

title: I get an error message saying, "H0007 Sentinel HSAP not found." How should I solve the problem?
content: **Question** I get an error message saying "H0007 Sentinel HSAP not found." How should I solve the problem? **Answer** This issue often occurs when the program cannot find the dongle key for authentication. Please refer to the [manual](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000615488#Click3) to learn how to solve the issue in detail.
content_description: This webpage provides solutions for resolving the "H0007 Sentinel HSAP not found" error related to dongle key authentication.

title: Do I need to configure my firewall to use CLO?
content: **Question** Do I need to configure my firewall to use CLO? **Answer** As long as you are connected to an internet, you can use CLO without configuring firewall. If you are using CLO for Enterprise and need to configure firewall due to company protocols, please [contact us](https://www.clo3d.com/contact).
content_description: This web page provides guidance on firewall configuration requirements for using CLO, clarifying that individual users can connect without adjustments, while enterprise users may need assistance based on company protocols.

title: Do I need to know 3D modeling in order to use CLO?
content: **Question** Do I need to know 3D modeling in order to use CLO? **Answer** No, CLO does not require any 3D modeling skills or any 3D software experience. However, prior experience with 3D software may increase your learning speed.
content_description: This web page aims to clarify that prior experience with 3D modeling is not necessary to use CLO, while noting that it may enhance the learning process.

title: Are there CLO offices located nearby?

title: Is 4K supported by CLO?
content: **Question** Is 4K supported by CLO? **Answer** Yes, 4K is supported by CLO from its ver4.0.0.

title: Does CLO offer a Linux version?
content: **Question** Does CLO offer a Linux version? **Answer** Unfortunately, CLO does not offer a Linux version and currently has no plan to develop one. If you find the Linux version of CLO is essential to your company, please post a request[ here](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/community/topics/115000546428-Product-Feedback). Our developers will review and rate the importance and priority for future new features.
content_description: This web page informs users that CLO does not currently offer a Linux version and provides a platform for feedback regarding the potential development of one.

title: Review Mode: How to use the Review data which saved in version 6.1 be used in version 6.2?
content: ## **Question** Are the Review Mode data (3D status info) saved in version 6.1 or earlier compatible with version 6.2? ## **Answer** From version 6.2, the simulation results by size have been improved to be applied directly to the review mode. Therefore, the 3D status info for the Review saved in version 6.1 or lower version is not compatible, and you need to re-simulate for each size. See below video also.
content_description: This web page aims to clarify the compatibility of Review Mode data between software versions 6.1 and 6.2, highlighting the need for re-simulation due to improved simulation results in the latest version.

title: Although my hardware has more than 4 CPU Cores, CLO is not as fast as I expected.
content: **Question** Although my hardware has more than 4 CPU cores, CLO is not as fast as I expected. **Answer** CLO's program speed increases with faster Core clock speed and more Cores. However, there is NO significant speed advancement when there are more than 4 Cores compared to the program speed ran with four Cores. Therefore, to be cost-effective, we recommend hardware with four Cores, each Core's speed being between 3.5 ~4.0 Ghz or faster.
content_description: This page aims to clarify the relationship between CPU core count and performance in CLO, recommending optimal hardware specifications for cost-effective efficiency.

title: CLO runs very slowly when I edit 3D Garment with Particle Distance 5. What should I do?
content: **Question** CLO runs very slowly when I edit 3D Garment with Particle Distance 5. What should I do? **Answer** For all 3D garment simulation programs, its simulation speed varies depending on the number of meshes in a single file. More meshes there are, slower the speed is. On the other hand, less meshes there are, faster the speed is. When Patterns' Particle Distance is set to 5, the program naturally slows down due to increase of the number of meshes in a single file. Therefore, we STRONGLY insist you to increase the Particle Distance to 20 when editing 3D Garments and decrease it to 5 when the 3D Garment is fully completed. Then, simulate for about 1~2 minutes. Does CLO still run slowly though Patterns' Particle Distance is set to 20? * This may happen when a Pattern is huge (e.g. flare skirt patterns,) because regardless of the Particle Distance value, bigger Patterns contain more meshes. * Also, due to difference in their intrinsic character, the program speed may reduce when Patterns' mesh structure is set to Quadrangular. Please refer to [Quadrangular/Triangular Mesh](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002727468-%EC%82%AC%EA%B0%81-%EB%A9%94%EC%8B%9C-%EC%82%BC%EA%B0%81-%EB%A9%94%EC%8B%9C) manual and configure mesh type as Quadrangular ONLY when needed. * Moreover, program speed is also influenced by hardware specification. Please check out suggested specification [here](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000307168-%EA%B6%8C%EC%9E%A5%EC%82%AC%EC%96%91).
content_description: This webpage provides guidance on optimizing CLO's performance when editing 3D garments by adjusting Particle Distance and understanding mesh impacts on simulation speed.

title: 3D File (COLLADA) Import
content: **Objective** COLLADA is a commonly used 3D application format that can be exported from 3D tools such as 3DS Max, Maya, Poser, and DAZ Studio and used as CLO Avatar or Scene/Prop. For 3DS Max or Maya, install the “OpenCOLLADA” plugin (<http://www.opencollada.org/download.html>) and use it to export in COLLADA format, instead of using the default COLLADA exporter. COLLADA files contain Geometry and Material, in addition to Rigging, Skinning, and Animation data. Avatar Motion Data can be imported into CLO in COLLADA file format, then saved as a *.mtn file, which is CLO's proprietary format. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ **OpenCOLLADA** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ **OpenCOLLADA** → The Open File window appears. 2. Select the desired file and click **OK**. → The Import COLLADA window opens. 3. Select the settings as needed and click **OK**. **Object Type** | **Import as Avatar** | Morphs the original object into the object designated as the Morph Target. Enter the Transition Frame count into the **Morphing Frame Count**. The higher the frame count, the slower the morphing process. ---|---|--- **Import as Prop/Scene** | Import the object as Scene and Props type **Scale** | Adjusts the scale of the file being imported when a value is entered **Garment Position** | **Move Garment to Start Position** | Moves the Avatar and Garment to the location of the first frame (ver2.5.0). ** ** **※ Note:** * If the COLLADA file path includes # (symbols), the file may not load properly. * In case of using Network Drive, copy a COLLADA file to local PC to open & use.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on importing COLLADA files into CLO, detailing the necessary steps and settings for successful integration of 3D assets as avatars or props.
